prompt: Rectangle $ABCD$ has side lengths $AB=10$ and $BC=12$. Let the midpoint of $CD$ be point $M$. Compute the area of the overlap between $\triangle AMB$ and $\triangle ADC$.

Let $\omega_1$ be the incircle of $\triangle ABC$ with side lengths $AB=AC=13$ and $BC=10$, and let $\omega_2$ be the circle inside $\triangle ABC$ that is externally tangent to $\omega_1$ and tangent to segments $AB$ and $AC$. Compute the radius of the circle inside $\triangle ABC$ that is externally tangent to $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ and tangent to segment $AB$.

solutions.title: Tangent circles along a side
solutions.body:
The area of $\triangle ABC$ is $60$ (height $12$), so $r_1=\frac{60}{18}=\frac{10}3$. Circle $\omega_2$ is the image of $\omega_1$ under a dilation about $A$, with ratio $\frac{12-2r_1}{12}$ (the altitude from $A$ is $12$ and $\omega_2$ sits above $\omega_1$ along it), so $r_2=\frac{12-20/3}{12}\cdot\frac{10}3=\frac{40}{27}$. Let $P_1,P_2$ be where $\omega_1,\omega_2$ touch $AB$; $AP_1=8$ (tangent length from $A$: $\frac{13+13-10}{2}$) and $AP_2=\frac{32}9$, so $P_1P_2=\frac{40}9$. A circle of radius $r$ tangent to $AB$ and externally tangent to a circle of radius $\rho$ that touches $AB$ has its center horizontally $2\sqrt{r\rho}$ from the touch point of that circle. The third circle lies between $P_1$ and $P_2$ along $AB$, so $2\sqrt{r\cdot\frac{10}{3}}+2\sqrt{r\cdot\frac{40}{27}}=\frac{40}{9}$. Thus $2\sqrt r\left(\sqrt{\frac{10}3}+\sqrt{\frac{40}{27}}\right)=\frac{40}9$; since $\sqrt{\frac{10}{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{30}}{3}$ and $\sqrt{\frac{40}{27}}=\frac{2\sqrt{30}}{9}$, the bracket is $\frac{5\sqrt{30}}9$, giving $\sqrt r=\frac{40/9}{2\cdot5\sqrt{30}/9}=\frac{4}{\sqrt{30}}=\frac{2\sqrt{30}}{15}$ and $r=\frac{120}{225}=\frac8{15}$.

**Answer: $\frac8{15}$**

prompt: Let circles $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ be circles with radii $6$ and $13$, respectively, such that the distance between their centers is $25$. A common external tangent touches $\omega_1$ at point $P$ and $\omega_2$ at point $Q$. A common internal tangent touches $\omega_1$ at point $R$ and $\omega_2$ at point $S$, and intersects line $PQ$ at point $T$ such that $TP<TQ$. Compute the length of segment $TR$.

solutions.title: Right angle at $T$
solutions.body:
Tangent lengths from $T$ give $TP=TR$ and $TQ=TS$, and $TO_1$, $TO_2$ bisect the angles of the two tangent pairs, so $\angle O_1TO_2=90^\circ$. The external tangent length is $PQ=\sqrt{25^2-7^2}=24$. Put $PQ$ on the $x$-axis, $P=(0,0)$, $Q=(24,0)$, $O_1=(0,6)$, $O_2=(24,13)$, $T=(t,0)$ with $t=TP$. The right angle gives $\overrightarrow{TO_1}\cdot\overrightarrow{TO_2}=(-t)(24-t)+6\cdot13=0$, i.e. $t^2-24t+78=0$, so $t=12\pm\sqrt{66}$. Since $TP<TQ$, $t<12$: $t=12-\sqrt{66}$, and $TR=TP=12-\sqrt{66}$.

**Answer: $12-\sqrt{66}$**
